excluded.test: guards.test.ts > custom guards > should provide the undefined params if a guard was configured using a string
excluded.reason: the only assertion is a spy's call argument, the params a guard named by a string receives (undefined); the oracle records no guard's call or params, no guard of the vocabulary named by a string can be evaluated without failing (every entry but fail needs params), and none tells undefined params apart from other params lacking its members. It would need a guard entry that answers whether its params are undefined, or a record of each guard's params

excluded.test: guards.test.ts > custom guards > should provide the guard with resolved params when they are dynamic
excluded.reason: the guard's params are a function (() => ({ stuff: 100 })) that XState resolves before calling the guard; a case's guard params are JSON handed to the guard as they are, with no computed form that becomes XState's params function, and the assertion reads the spy's call argument, while the oracle records no guard's call or params. It would need computed guard params (resolved by XState as the params function, and by xstate likewise) and a guard entry that exposes the params it received

excluded.test: guards.test.ts > guards - other > inline function guard should not leak into provided guards object
excluded.reason: the only assertion is that the guards object the test hands createMachine is still {} after the inline function guard () => false was evaluated (XState must not register the inline guard in it); a case hands XState no implementations object of its own (the guards are the vocabulary's fixed table, and an inline function guard is not JSON), and the oracle records neither the implementations nor any change to them, while xstate's create_machine takes its implementations by value, so a caller's copy has nothing to observe.
